hook_text: One confused sentence at a press conference opened a wall that had stood for twenty-eight years.
clip_script: Berlin, 9 November 1989. For twenty-eight years a wall has split this city. But the Soviet Union is running out of money, and its leader, Gorbachev, has told Eastern Europe: choose your own way. Poland votes out the communists. Hungary cuts its border fence. In Leipzig, crowds march every Monday chanting, we are the people. Then, at a live press conference, an East German official reads out new travel rules. A journalist asks: when do they start? He checks his notes. Immediately. Thousands rush to the Wall. One guard, no orders, a huge crowd. At half past eleven, he opens the gate. Strangers hug. People dance on the concrete with hammers. Less than a year later, Germany is one country again. And in South Africa, three months later, the ANC is unbanned.
visual_style: A grainy television screen showing a man reading from notes; crowds with candles in Leipzig; a checkpoint barrier lifting under floodlights; people standing on the Wall at the Brandenburg Gate swinging hammers; a newspaper headline about Mandela's release.
pacing: Building tension through the press conference, bursting into celebration at the open gate.
